title: Measure: live field views, real measurements and saved outputs
description: Use the downloadable sixteen-field example to inspect live fields and channels, restore raw-crop settings, read quality warnings, run with Plot enabled and verify saved measurements.
objectives: Load the current Measure example and distinguish intensity channels from label-mask planes.
Inspect fields and channels live, distinguish the view selector from shared crop settings, and restore normalization before the batch.
Run the full example, inspect real figures and console output, and locate verified measurements and crop files.
Find the nested Illumination, AnnData Export and Motility workflows and understand the limits of the AI console and stale-output warning.
prerequisite: Open Measure from Home/Core and use Load test data. The measured subset is sixteen 1994x1994 merged uint16 arrays: intensity planes 0–3 and mask planes 4/5/6 for cells/nuclei/pathogen objects. Before the first Live preview, enable the main Normalize toggle; the panel initializes contrast at percentiles 1/99. Do not Run with that toggle on. Channel zero is a view-only choice, but the main Normalize setting also concerns saved crops. Turn Live off and restore Normalize off before running. The preview shows 27 objects in E02_1_1 and 15 in E02_9_1; channel changes preserve labels, areas and categories, and restoring All channels restores the original pixels. Preview and batch source arrays are byte-identical. Crop settings is oversized in this build; inaccessible normalization/propagation/filter-dialog scenes are deliberately not taught as usable. The background QC banner flags 3 failures and 16 warnings across 156 object-field records from the larger 52-field mask download, not just the 16 merged fields measured here. The data are illustrative, not certified clean. The full run uses Plot on, Test mode off, one worker, save_measurements/save_png on, normalize off and RGB224x224 cell crops. With no voxel calibration, areas are pixels squared. Independent checks cover 5409 area/intensity values including five source-supported label merges, not every feature or biological correctness. Outputs: 601 cell records/crops, 622 nuclei, 373 pathogen objects, 48 saved plots (47 in the GUI queue). Runtime-added hash_inputs and _intensity_rescale_plan cause this run's stale-output warning; arbitrary warnings and automatic handoff are not certified safe. A separate test-mode run registered the wrong database path; this lesson uses verified normal-mode outputs. API: spacr.measure.measure_crop. See Illumination, Motility and AnnData Export separately; AnnData teaches an explicit API workaround, not a repaired GUI. No AI question is sent, no response is demonstrated, and no human listening approval or publication is claimed.

scenes.narration: Open Measure from the Core modules. It turns existing image arrays and object masks into measurements and crops; it does not create a new segmentation. Illumination, AnnData Export and Motility are nested workflows under this main module. Their separate lessons belong under Measure in the tutorial navigation.

Choose Load test data and wait for the actual example to finish loading. This download supplies sixteen merged fields. Check the source folder and channel mapping: intensity channels zero to three, cell mask four, nucleus mask five, and pathogen mask six. Mask labels are not intensity measurements.

Before opening Live for the first time, search for Normalize in the main settings and turn it on. This initializes a readable preview because the raw sixteen-bit crops look dark. This is also a saved-crop setting, not just a display preference. Do not press Run; we will restore it first.

Switch Live on and paste the merged-array path for field E zero two, one, one. The grid shows twenty-seven candidates, grouped by mask relationships; scroll to inspect the remaining categories. These labels are not independently reviewed biological annotations, and displayed candidates are not a promise of the final measured-cell count.

Choose channel zero in the displayed-channel selector. The same twenty-seven objects now appear in grayscale; their labels, areas and categories are unchanged. Unlike the main Normalize setting, this selector changes only the preview view. Return to All channels to restore the original color pixels without changing the batch settings.

Use the field selector to open E zero two, nine, one. This field has fifteen displayed candidates: inspect more than one field before trusting an attractive image. Also read the red segmentation-quality banner. Its flagged masks come from the larger downloaded set; successful preview rendering does not resolve those warnings or certify clean data.

Turn Live off, search for Normalize again, and switch it off before running. We verified that all batch settings return to their original values and both source arrays remain unchanged. Per-crop normalization can remove intensity differences from saved images. Keep the original arrays; this lesson does not use the oversized Crop settings dialog.

Keep Plot enabled, save measurements and crops, and use one worker for this demonstration. Test mode is off: this run processes all sixteen example fields into the main project output. A short test uses a separate test folder in this build, so do not confuse its database with the full-run result.

Press Run and follow the console. Check the attempted, succeeded and failed counts, not merely the presence of a finished message. Here all sixteen fields succeeded. Large plots can trigger an explicit export-resolution limit; read that warning as well. A successfully completed computation is not a biological quality certificate.

Use the figure list to inspect the actual before-filtering and after-filtering views. Drag the divider to give the figures more room. Size filters and parent-child merging can change which labels are measured. In this example, five saved cell objects combine source labels connected by a shared nucleus or pathogen mask.

Inspect the crop figure too, then keep the measurements database and its image paths together. This run saved six hundred one cell records and matching crops. Independent pixel checks verified area and four-channel intensity sums and means, including those merges; this does not validate every feature or the segmentation's biological correctness.

This build can still display a stale-output warning after a successful run with unchanged visible settings. We traced this example to runtime-added metadata, but have not fixed the application. Verify the actual saved run and settings before continuing; do not dismiss other warnings or assume that automatic handoff has been validated. Also check the files: this recording's figure queue showed forty-seven of forty-eight saved plots.

The console also offers optional spaCR AI assistance. Here we enable the toggle and prepare a question without sending it, so no answer or external analysis is demonstrated. Treat any later response as advice to verify against the settings, API and saved results. Use the separate nested-workflow lessons for the next task.
